To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

four clinical variables (hospital acquisition, antibiotic treatment before bacteremia, endotrachealed intubation, thermal trauma), combined in an index (PI), predict the susceptibility of gram-negative bacteria in bacteremic patients.
the performance of the index in predicting the antibiotic resistance of gram-negative isolates is good and that the index can help in the choice of an empiric antibiotic regimen.

a predictive index, based on four clinical variables, can be used to identify patients at high risk of multiresistant gram-negative bacilli, and to improve empiric treatment in patients with bacteremia caused by these bacteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a predictive index for the optimization of empiric antibiotic treatment of gram-negative bacillary bacteremia.
the development of a simple index that can predict the likelihood that a gram-negative isolate from a patient with bacteremia will be multiresistant to commonly used antibiotics.

the development of a simple and inexpensive tool that may help the attending physician in the empiric treatment of bacteremic patients, and may help in the rationalization of the use of antibiotics in the hospital.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed index is a useful tool for the clinician to predict which gram-negative isolates will be multiresistant, and to optimize the empiric treatment of patients with gram-negative bacteremia.
the index is not a substitute for clinical judgment, but rather a tool to improve it.
the index can be used to optimize empiric treatment in patients with gram-negative bacteremia, but only when combined with the knowledge of local resistance patterns.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in patients with a high risk of multiresistant bacteria, the choice of empiric antibiotics should be guided by a knowledge of the most common multiresistant gram-negative bacteria in each hospital and of the resistance patterns of those bacteria.

the index could probably help in the selection of empiric antibiotic treatment, and that the index could also serve as a basis for a prospective study to evaluate the impact of antibiotic policy on the emergence of multiresistant gram-negative bacteria.
the clinical index is a useful tool for predicting resistance to antibiotics, and that the index could be used to guide empiric treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a predictive index for optimizing empirically the treatment of gram-negative infections can be developed and validated.

a clinical score can be used to identify patients who are at high risk of acquiring infections due to multiresistant strains and who therefore should be given empiric treatment with broad spectrum antibiotic regimens.
clinicians should be cautious when using antibiotics to treat gram-negative bacteremias, especially in patients with a high index score.
